problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ be bases of ${R}^{2}.$ If ${b}_{1}=2{c}_{2}-2{c}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}={c}_{1}-2{c}_{2},$ find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{B\to C}$ from $B$ to $C.$

feedback.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B$ to the basis $C$ is given by 
${P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}4 & -7 \\ 3 & -5\end{aligned}].$
Find the change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B$  .
feedback.worked_solution:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B$ is the inverse of the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C.$ Therefore, we simply need to find the inverse of the given matrix.

Computing the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & -7 \\ 3 & -5\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\cdot (-5)-(-7)\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}-5 & 7 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =1\cdot [\begin{aligned}-5 & 7 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 7 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
